title: P0 hosted-api: prefetch-queue filibuster — postmortem and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

On 2029-04-05 08:12 UTC we observed a sustained p95/p99 streaming latency and a burst of 5xx errors affecting ~18% of hosted-api streaming sessions for ~38 minutes. Root cause: a pathological interaction between the prefetch worker pool and adaptive batching heuristics that caused long-running prefetch tasks to occupy the limited prefetch queue (the "prefetch queue filibuster"). This starved fresh requests of prefetch capacity and caused tail latency to climb while head requests retried, producing cascading backpressure into the streaming multiplexer.

Customer impact:
- Affected customers: all regions; traffic routed to region-us-central experienced the worst effects.
- Symptoms: streaming responses stalled then either 5xx'd or resumed after multi-second gaps, increased reconnects, client-level timeouts.
- Duration: 2029-04-05 08:12 UTC -> 2029-04-05 08:50 UTC (mitigations stage), residual elevated p95 until 09:15 UTC while autoscaler recovered.
- Severity: P0 (external user impact, increased error budgets, business-critical SLAs degraded).

Timeline (high-level):
- 08:11: alert fired: streaming p95 > latency-slo threshold (SLO-alarm-STREAM-P95)
- 08:12: oncall paged (pager duty). First responder (Aisha) triaged from SRE dashboard.
- 08:13-08:20: quick triage: discovered growing prefetch-queue depth on region-us-central hostpool (metric: prefetch.queue.depth per-host ~ >95th percentile).
- 08:20: rolled temporary mitigation: increased prefetch-worker concurrency on hot machines (+2 workers) and drained the longest-running queue entries.
- 08:28: still elevated; applied second mitigation: disabled prefetch for low-priority routes (route tag: debug, internal).
- 08:35: observed partial recovery; but some sessions still 5xx due to acceptor backpressure.
- 08:42: rolled global throttling tweak (reduce adaptive-batch window from 1.8s to 1.0s) to prevent oversized prefetch tasks.
- 08:50: p95 back within SLO for most regions; full stabilization completed by 09:15 after autoscaler rebalanced.

Detection and signals used:
- Primary: streaming p95 and p99 alerts from telemetry (datapipeline:streaming.latency.p95)
- Secondary: prefetch.queue.depth, prefetch.worker.task-duration histogram, acceptor.queue-length, connector-reconnect-rate, pod CPU/EBS metrics.
- Human signals: increased Slack noise, customer tickets (CS-TKT-4821), and SDK reconnect patterns.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis -> evidence -> conclusion):
1) Hypothesis: A recent change in adaptive batching (PR #1875) widened the batching window for low-throughput sessions; combined with a regression in prefetch task TTL allowed long-lived prefetch tasks to remain in queue.
   Evidence:
   - Deployment timeline: PR #1875 merged 2029-04-04 and promoted to canary 2029-04-04 23:00 UTC, global rollout 2029-04-05 07:40 UTC.
   - Metric correlation: prefetch.task-duration 99th percentile spiked after rollout; long-tail tasks were occupying queue slots.
   - Logs: dozens of prefetch worker logs showing tasks stuck >30s with repeated KV read retries.
   Conclusion: rollout exposed previously rare workload patterns where prefetch tasks repeatedly retried on transient KV lease contention; the widened batching window amplified these tasks' work size, making them long-running.

2) Hypothesis: Prefetch queue has low headroom (configured depth 8) which is insufficient when a subset of tasks become long-running.
   Evidence:
   - Observed queue depth = 8/8 on many hosts; backlog metrics show >60% of hosts saturated for ~20 minutes.
   - Runbook config shows conservative default (8) chosen historically to limit memory/CPU per-host.
   Conclusion: queue depth was too small to tolerate a minority of long-lived tasks; lack of bounded task TTL allowed queue saturation to escalate into service-level impact.

Immediate mitigations applied (what we did during the incident):
- Increased per-host prefetch worker count by +2 on the affected hostpool to increase headroom (rolled within 4 minutes).
- Disabled prefetch for labeled low-priority routes to free queue slots (8 minutes).
- Tuned adaptive batching window down from 1.8s -> 1.0s to reduce generated prefetch load (30 minutes).
- KVI (kv-interface) retry backoff adjusted temporarily to avoid tight retry loops (hotfix container rollback-style change).

Why mitigations helped:
- More workers + disabled prefetch freed immediate queue capacity allowing critical new requests to be serviced.
- Reducing batch window reduced amount of speculative prefetch work produced per request, lowering new long-lived tasks creation.

Permanent root cause(s):
- Combined config regression: adaptive batch window increase + missing task TTL for prefetch tasks + conservative queue depth limit.
- Prefetch tasks retried too aggressively under transient KV contention due to tight retry policy.

Action items (short/medium/long-term) — owners and target dates:
- Short (<=1 week):
  - Add task-level TTL for prefetch tasks so they cancel after 6s if not started. Owner: Mei Chen. Due: 2029-04-12.
  - Patch adaptive batching config to include safety cap on work-per-request. Owner: Ben Rodriguez. Due: 2029-04-10.
  - Update runbook with a "prefetch saturation" mitigation checklist (increase workers, disable low-priority prefetch, backoff tweak). Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2029-04-09.
- Medium (<=1 month):
  - Increase default prefetch queue depth from 8 -> 16 with memory/CPU guardrails and autoscaling tests. Owner: Omar Vaziri. Due: 2029-05-05.
  - Implement sentinel metric and alert for prefetch.task-duration p95>5s with correlated queue depth >0. Owner: Riley Park. Due: 2029-04-20.
- Long (<=3 months):
  - Introduce prefetch admission control that prioritizes new requests over speculative work and evicts low-priority speculative tasks under pressure. Owner: Runtime team (RFC + implementation). Due: 2029-07-05.
  - Improve KV lease backoff and retry strategy to avoid repeated hot loops. Owner: Applied ML infra. Due: 2029-07-05.

Runbook draft (prefetch-saturation section) — emergency steps (short):
1) Identify affected hostpool: run dashboard query: prefetch.queue.depth by hostpool for last 5m.
2) If >60% hosts saturated: increase prefetch workers on hostpool by +2 (hotpatch via infra autoproc; command: infractl pool scale --name <hostpool> --prefetch-workers +2).
3) Disable prefetch for low-priority routes: config toggle label prefetch=off for route-tags: internal, debug.
4) If still not recovered: temporarily reduce adaptive-batch.window to 1.0s (config push), roll back PR if a recent rollout is suspected.
5) If acceptor backlog increases: temporarily enable global throttling to keep client-facing error rates within SLO until prefetch queue drains.
6) Post-incident: collect traces, prefetch task histograms, and export last 1h logs for affected hosts.

Notes to self / on-call learnings (informal):
- The prefetch subsystem had been functioning with low variability for months — the regression came from a seemingly benign change to batching heuristics. We need stronger safety nets on canary rollouts for subsystems that generate speculative background work.
- Pager hand-off: make sure next oncall has the prefetch runbook link and the quick mitigation commands in the PD page.
- Customer communication: CS drafted a short note summarizing impact and mitigation; coordinate before sending final.

Data and artifacts collected (for postmortem):
- Host-level metrics: prefetch.queue.depth, prefetch.worker.count, prefetch.task-duration histograms (collected).
- Traces: 142 representative streaming traces we captured (trace IDs attached in linked_artifacts).
- Logs: aggregated prefetch worker logs (S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2029-04-05/prefetch-filibuster/).
- Ticket links: Linear SRE-3214, CS-TKT-4821.

Unresolved questions / open investigations:
- Why did KV lease contention spikes occur at the same time? Hypothesis: brief shard rebalances in KV cluster; ignore unlikely but still investigating with storage team. (Assigned to Mei)
- Did any tenant-specific workload exacerbate the problem (heavy long-context sessions)? (Assigned to Solutions Eng: Riley).

Follow-ups planned (owner meeting items):
- 2029-04-08 16:00 UTC post-incident sync with runtime, applied-ml infra, and storage teams to agree on TTL, queue sizing, and KV retry policy.
- Postmortem write-up to finalize (this doc) with full timeline + timelines of config changes; target final release 2029-04-10.

Appendix: quick commands used during incident (notes)
- check queue depth: kq metric query "fetch_prefetch_queue_depth{hostpool="us-central"}" --last 5m
- increase workers (infra hotpatch): infractl pool scale --name us-central --prefetch-workers +2 --reason "incident 2029-04-05"
- toggle prefetch: cfgctl set route-tag prefetch=off --tags internal,debug --env hosted-api
- rollback PR: deployctl rollback runtime-service --commit-before sha:abc123 --reason "incident mitigation"

Acknowledgements:
- First responders: Ben R., Mei C., Omar V., Riley P., + oncall backups. Thanks for rapid coordination and crisp execution on mitigations.
